name: Antarctic Science Foundation
quote: “Antarctica offers us the answers. Let’s ask the questions together.”
description:
Antarctica

The Antarctic Science Foundation is a “for-impact” organisation that brings together all people who believe in the value and potential of Antarctica to provide the answers we need to sustain our way of life on this planet.

The Problem

Antarctica and the Southern Ocean are the global engine room of Earth’s climate, profoundly influencing weather systems through its oceans and atmosphere. For more than 50 million years, they have acted as shock absorbers, gathering heat and carbon in the ocean, while the white continent reflects heat and radiation back into space.

At twice the size of Australia, this wild, pristine continent is now humanity’s “canary in the coal mine” and the focus of considerable change. Our challenge is to shape our future by listening and discovering what we need to know in the present.

The Solution

When you support the Antarctic Science Foundation, you will be backing dedicated, tenacious researchers to be curious as they confront uncertainty in the most extreme conditions. You will support these scientists to ask the important questions to sustain our way of life through tangible outcomes in:

  • Climate prediction for all Australians, living in our cities and those who live on the land
  • Fire, flood and drought prediction and mitigation
  • Managing economic and sustainable fisheries
  • Carbon capture and abatement via nature’s systems
  • Increasing the health of our oceans
  • Improving global biodiversity
  • Protection of Antarctic wildlife 

What difference will your money make?

$28 provides spatial analysis of a penguin’s breeding habits.

$95 provides for seawater analysis to understand impact of climate change on plankton and krill.

$270 provides a data-analysis session, a vital input models of interaction to develop climate change mitigation strategies.

$480 provides a seal tracker which will assist mapping of the undersides of ice-shelves.

$980 provides a marine probe to assess changes in whale habitats.
